teaser: Ever heard someone say 'that's just鸡毛蒜皮'? Let's explore this colorful idiom together.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever heard someone say 'that's just鸡毛蒜皮'? Let's explore this colorful idiom together.[break 1s]The phrase is: 鸡毛蒜皮, jī máo suàn pí.[break 0.5s]鸡 (jī) - chicken [break 0.5s]毛 (máo) - feather [break 0.5s]蒜 (suàn) - garlic [break 0.5s]皮 (pí) - skin [break 1s]So, 鸡毛蒜皮 literally means 'chicken feathers and garlic skins' and figuratively refers to trivial matters or insignificant details.[break 1s]Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s]In ancient times, people would often engage in debates about the importance of various items. One day, a philosopher observed that people were wasting time arguing over things as inconsequential as chicken feathers and garlic skins. He used this observation to warn others about the dangers of focusing on trivial matters instead of more meaningful issues.[break 1.5s]Example 1: 这件事完全是鸡毛蒜皮。[break 1s]This matter is completely trivial. [break 1s]Example 2: 不要为这些鸡毛蒜皮的事情争论。[break 1s]Don't argue over these insignificant issues. [break 1s]Example 3: 他的抱怨都是鸡毛蒜皮。[break 1s]His complaints are all about trivial matters. [break 1s]So, 鸡毛蒜皮 means trivial matters or insignificant details. Thank you for listening, and see you next time for another idiom! [break 1s]
